- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >65), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (≥ 0.0), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for first 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model exhibits mean reversion bias; add 0.3–0.7% upward correction after 3 consecutive negative sentiment days.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in mid-horizon (days 15–25); apply 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment for days 15–25 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
